title: River nutrients to the Gulf
text: The Mississippi drains about 41% of the continental US. Its nitrogen and phosphorus, mostly from farm runoff and sewage, feed the algal blooms behind the Gulf's summer dead zone. Wikipedia, citing a NOAA fact sheet, attributes about 70% of the nutrient load to this basin.
when: Flows all year; spring floods bring the biggest load, and the dead zone is largest in summer.
matters: Too much nitrogen and phosphorus feeds algae. When the algae die and rot they use up oxygen near the sea floor, and fish and shellfish leave or die.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Gulf of Mexico dead zone
